# Jubilees Chapter 4 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 4:5 — Response to the heavenly tablet curse: "So be it" vs. "Amen"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "let all who have seen and heard say, So be it" | Literal Ge'ez response particle |
| LOGOS | "let all who have seen or heard say, Amen" | "Amen" is the recognized cognate in Jewish liturgical context |
| PNEUMA | "Let everyone who witnessed it say, 'So be it'" | Keeps "So be it" as modern equivalent |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS "Amen." The Ge'ez particle here (amen/ameha) is the standard liturgical response; "Amen" communicates both accuracy and liturgical resonance. "So be it" is a valid paraphrase but loses the cultic register.

---

## 4:16 — Enoch as inventor of writing

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the first among men that are born on earth who learned writing and knowledge and wisdom" | Literal order |
| LOGOS | "the first among men born on earth to learn writing and knowledge and wisdom" | Formal, same content |
| PNEUMA | "the first human being born on earth to master writing, knowledge, and wisdom" | "Master" implies achievement more strongly |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Learn" accurately represents the Ge'ez verb; "master" (PNEUMA) adds a connotation not directly in the source, though defensible in context.

---

## 4:22 — Enoch's translation to Eden

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "we conducted him into the garden of Eden in majesty and honor" | "Conducted" = formally escorted |
| LOGOS | "we brought him into the garden of Eden with great honor" | "Brought" is simpler; "great honor" |
| PNEUMA | "the angels escorted him into the garden of Eden in great honor" | Shifts to third person |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Brought him into the garden of Eden with great honor" is accurate and readable. Retaining first-person "we" (vs. PNEUMA's "the angels") preserves the angelic narrative voice of Jubilees.

---

## 4:29 — Adam's age and the one-day = 1000 years equation

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "He lacked seventy years of one thousand years; for one thousand years are as one day in the testimony of the heavens" | Fully literal |
| LOGOS | "He lacked seventy years of one thousand years, for one thousand years are as one day in the testimony of the heavens" | Identical to EMET — strong agreement |
| PNEUMA | "He fell seventy years short of a thousand. And a thousand years is equivalent to one day in the reckoning of heaven." | Paraphrased: "reckoning of heaven" for "testimony of the heavens" |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS/EMET (identical). "Testimony of the heavens" is the Jubilees technical term (drawing on Ps 90:4); "reckoning" (PNEUMA) loses the covenantal/legal register of "testimony."

---

## 4:27 — Noah's name etymology

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "This one will comfort me from my work and from my toil of my hands in the earth" | Follows the Gen 5:29 etymology literally |
| LOGOS | "This one will comfort us in our work and in the toil of our hands on the earth" | "us" rather than "me" — Jubilees shifts to communal |
| PNEUMA | "This one will bring us relief from all the hard work and exhaustion this cursed earth has cost us" | "Relief" and "exhaustion" paraphrase |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Comfort us" reflects the Jubilees Ge'ez plural (communal consolation), whereas EMET's "me" follows a different tradition. PNEUMA's "relief" and "exhaustion" over-paraphrase the Semitic name-etymology formula.

---

**Total disagreements: 5**
